name: Kami
tagline: MIT layout rules and templates for agents exporting PDF, PNG, and PPTX
description:
Kami is an agent skill by Tw93. The README says the name means paper, and that it gives agents layout rules and templates for PDF, PNG, and editable PowerPoint. It lists eight document templates: One-Pager, Long Doc, Letter, Portfolio, Resume, Slides, Equity Report, and Changelog, plus a landing-page system, in English, Chinese, and Korean. It also describes eighteen inline SVG diagram types, WeasyPrint for PDF, python-pptx for editable PPTX, and a zero-dependency MCP server in skills/kami/scripts/mcp_server.py.

The install line is npx skills add tw93/kami -a claude-code codex cursor -g -y. The LICENSE file is MIT, copyright 2026 Tw93. The README says large CJK fonts stay out of the package and that Windows should run Kami inside WSL.
install: npx skills add tw93/kami -a claude-code codex cursor -g -y
agent_guidance:
Install with npx skills add tw93/kami -a claude-code codex cursor -g -y. The README says that lands one copy in ~/.agents/skills. On Windows, use WSL. The helper scripts are Bash.

The code and templates are MIT. Default colors in the README are a parchment background #f5f4ed and ink #1B365D. Put brand overrides in ~/.config/kami/brand.md rather than editing the templates for one project.
why_it_matters: It gives an agent a documented way to export a designed PDF or an editable deck, not only a markdown file.
tier_reason: MIT, a specific install command, templates named in the README, and a push on the day of this check.
evidence: Checked the GitHub page, raw README, and raw LICENSE for tw93/Kami on 2026-10-25. The LICENSE file is MIT. The README states the install command, the eight templates, the MCP script path, and the Windows note. GitHub API reported 12,077 stars and a push on 2026-10-25. Source tweet: https://x.com/HiTw93/status/2094792220155285685.

tagline: Motion-design gallery with animated components, shaders, and a linked MIT-0 component repo
description:

name: HandDrawnFont
tagline: SwiftUI package for animated hand-drawn text, Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause
description:
HandDrawnFont is a SwiftUI package that renders text from pen strokes. The site says letters come from the original pen paths, animation keeps stroke order, and the package respects Reduce Motion. It is made by Jip van der Velde and Michel Elings at Ocho, the makers of grug. The site says grug won a 2026 Apple Design Award. Install is through Swift Package Manager from the GitHub repository, with import HandDrawnFont and a HandDrawnText view.

The LICENSE file is Apache License 2.0 subject to the Commons Clause. The clause covers selling a product or service whose value derives entirely or substantially from HandDrawnFont, including the bundled Grug Hand stroke artwork and font files. It says drawings a user makes in the font creator are excluded. GitHub's license API returns NOASSERTION.
pricing_detail: No price on the site. The LICENSE file is Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause, which restricts selling a product whose value derives from the software, including the bundled Grug Hand artwork.
agent_guidance:
Add the GitHub repository in Swift Package Manager and render HandDrawnText. The site says Reduce Motion is respected. Keep that path.

Do not sell a product whose value comes from this package. The LICENSE file adds the Commons Clause on top of Apache 2.0, and it includes the bundled Grug Hand artwork. A font the user draws in the creator is excluded from that clause. The last GitHub push was 2026-09-03.
why_it_matters: It draws real pen paths in SwiftUI, with the stroke order intact, under a license that limits resale.
tier_reason: The package, the Reduce Motion claim, and the license text were checked. The Commons Clause means it is not a plain Apache grant, and the last push was September 2026.
evidence: Checked https://handdrawn.software/ and the raw README and LICENSE for jipvandervelde/HandDrawnFont on 2026-10-25. The site states Swift Package Manager, Reduce Motion, and the Ocho / grug credit. The LICENSE file is Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause v1.0. GitHub API reported 90 stars, license NOASSERTION, and a push on 2026-09-03. Source tweet: https://x.com/grug_speak/status/2092510233830506824.
